title: UK retail sales, Great Britain — August 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the base steps down, and the print lands on September quad-witching
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/retailsalesgreatbritainaugust2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200) for this canonical write — the release page reads 'Retail Sales; Great Britain: August 2026', '18 September 2026 at 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', and states these are accredited official statistics independently reviewed by the Office for Statistics Regulation. Corroborated the same day by the July-2026 bulletin's own 'Next release: 18 September 2026' line (ons.gov.uk/businessindustryandtrade/retailindustry/bulletins/retailsales/latest, fetched direct 2026-09-15). Originally discovered 2026-09-10 by two sibling lanes independently, whose proposals (proposals/uk-retail-sales-2026-09-18.from-uk-retail-sales-2026-10-23.json and .from-uk-retail-sales-2026-12-18.json) were read in full before this file was written. Stays estimate on two counts, neither of them doubt about the date: this lane may not self-confirm an event, and market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has CENSUS: for the US retail print and no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-15 by the uk-retail-sales-2026-09-18 never-assessed lane from TWO independent proposals, both dated 2026-09-10, both reproducing the same release page. The 10-23 lane proposed it because this print is the single largest mover of that ledger's arithmetic: it resolves one of the two unknown monthly clears in the September annual rate AND restates the July 2026 index that ledger's carry is measured from. The 12-18 lane proposed it because 2026-09-18 is the third Friday of September and therefore US quad-witching, reproducing 91 days early the exact ONS-print-into-a-witching-session configuration that the December entry is about. Both reasons survive research and are recorded in docs/research/events/uk-retail-sales-2026-09-18.md. WHAT THIS ENTRY IS ABOUT, IN ONE LINE: the annual base steps DOWN from July 2025 (102.1) to August 2025 (101.6) in ONS series J5EK, so a flat month mechanically adds ~0.49pp to the annual rate — this print is expected to read as an ACCELERATION from July's +1.6% in the same month the BRC-KPMG panel called the weakest since October 2024. The acceleration, if it lands, is base arithmetic and not a consumer revival, and any recap saying otherwise is wrong. NAME COLLISION, WORTH ONE SENTENCE IN ANY RECAP: retail-sales-2026-09-16 is the US Census advance print two days earlier, tiered high; this is Great Britain — a different publisher and a different concept (GB volumes, seasonally adjusted, versus US nominal receipts). Expected LOW on the same measured grounds as every UK sibling: symbols [], no UK-listed name in this book, no sterling- or rates-keyed house playbook. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
